headline: Scaling functional annotation beyond sequence similarity across genomes and metagenomes
label: Genome Scale Functional Annotation Methods
summary: Recent tools extend homology-based and structure-based annotation to pangenomes, unannotated assemblies and global metagenomes.
synthesis: The common thread is annotation that extends beyond direct sequence similarity, using predicted structures, genomic context, taxonomic linkage and targeted search to assign function across pangenomes, assemblies and metagenomes. Sma3s v3 combines MMseqs2 with caching and taxonomic filtering to annotate 60.8% of a Vibrio cholerae pangenome. Vritra builds gene-specific references from UniRef linked to taxonomy for species-resolved metagenomic and metatranscriptomic profiling. A structure-based pipeline over 5.1M oral microbiome proteins yields 20 new protein kinase-like domains, while a marine CAZyme resource of about 290,000 gene clusters from over 22,000 MAGs supports polysaccharide utilization analysis. fDOG-Assembly performs feature-aware ortholog search directly in unannotated assemblies, matching BUSCO and Compleasm performance. A global metagenomic analysis identifies about 6.5 million putative protein families using AlphaFold2 structures and gene-neighborhood information. What is new is the combination of structural prediction and genomic context applied at this scale.
